question: 60. Consider the set $S$ of all integers between and including 1000 and 99999. Call two integers $x$ and $y$ in $S$ to be in the same equivalence class if the digits appearing in $x$ and $y$ are the same. For example, if $x=1010$, $y=1000$ and $z=1201$, then $x$ and $y$ are in the same equivalence class, but $y$ and $z$ are not. Find the number of distinct equivalence classes that can be formed out of $S$.
